core_idea: Classify each pile by its least-significant-set-bit position. The minimum position determines whether the first player can force a win, the second player wins, or both can perpetually preserve a mixed state and draw; then count configurations by these categories.
reasoning_patterns: Use 2-adic valuation / lsb positions as the game state invariant.
When all lsb positions are equal to c, every move reduces all of them to c-1.
If the minimum lsb is odd, choosing a minimum pile creates an equal even-lsb state for the opponent, which is losing.
If the minimum lsb is even and every pile has that lsb, every move creates an equal odd-lsb state for the opponent, so the current player loses.
If the minimum lsb is even but lsb values are mixed, choosing a pile above the minimum preserves both a minimum-lsb pile and a higher-lsb pile, enabling an infinite draw.
Count arrays with minimum lsb exactly i via a difference of powers: (2^(K-i)-1)^N - (2^(K-i-1)-1)^N.
